opens the downloaded copy
when there is one and streams the edition otherwise, so the screen needs
no offline logic of its own. The screen shows a spinner until the edition
reports progress, then a progress bar: a streamed edition reports progress
as its opening pages download, and a downloaded one opens without
reporting any. When opening fails, the screen hides both and offers a
retry. Opening has no side effects to undo, so retrying is calling it
again.

Reports collapse progress (0 = expanded … 1 = collapsed) per frame in every
mode: interactive scrubs track the finger, and non-interactive settles (release,
programmatic show/hide) are driven by a display link that scrubs the same
animator — so this fires from the same write that moves the chrome, keeping
consumers in sync by construction. Only invoked when the value actually changes,
so steady-state scrolling (fully expanded or fully collapsed) publishes nothing.
